key_insight: Standardizing prostate cancer EHR data to OMOP and adding NLP plus PSA-based algorithms substantially improved capture of key clinical details and research readiness.
clinical_relevance: This approach can help researchers build more complete prostate cancer datasets for real-world studies, while also flagging missing or inconsistent registry/EHR information.
method: Converted UTMB Epic EHR records for registry-identified prostate cancer patients into OMOP CDM v5.4.
Used NLP to extract PSA, Gleason score, and cancer stage from clinical text.
Applied PSA-based algorithms to identify missing treatment data and biochemical recurrence.
evidence_signal: Among 815 analytic cases, 700 (85.9%) were complete and concordant with the cancer registry, PSA agreement was excellent, and NLP substantially improved capture of sparse Gleason score and stage data.
watch_item: Findings come from a single health system and some key fields were sparse in structured EHR data, so performance may vary when scaled to other sites or data models.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
